Test Case: The process for an article to become a 'Featured Article' on Wikipedia is a rigorous and lengthy peer review journey. Long before appearing on the front page, the article must undergo a separate peer review to improve its quality significantly. For instance, some articles might be part of the 'Medicine Collaboration of the Week' project to ensure accuracy in health topics. Once nominated as a Featured Article Candidate, or FAC, a consensus must be reached by the community that it meets all the strict criteria. The community has developed specific style guidelines to ensure that facts appear in a standardized and professional form. During the FAC review, any user is allowed to participate and provide votes of support or opposition. However, any objections raised must be actionable, meaning there must be a clear way to address the concern. If the concerns are not resolved, the FA Director may decide to remove the nomination from the list. This complex and bureaucratic process runs counter to the naive idea that Wikipedia is an anarchic space. Even after promotion, articles can be demoted if their quality falls below the ever-increasing standards over time.
